record.context_brief: Optimality of the Robin-setting L^{q**} a priori bounds
record.original_question: For the generalized Robin boundary-value problem in which the a priori L^{q**} bounds are derived from an embedding of D(a_S) into L^p(Omega) together with Moser iteration, are those resulting L^{q**} a priori bounds best possible?

evidence.quote: Remark 12. One could ask if the Lq** a priori bounds derived from (24) by Moser iteration are the best possible. Indeed they are: [Dan00, Theorem 5.11.].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ ($N \geq 2$) be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary $\partial\Omega$, and let $\sigma$ denote the $(N-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\partial\Omega$. Consider the generalized Robin boundary value problem
$$
-\operatorname{div}(A(x)\nabla u) + a_0(x)\, u = f(x) \quad \text{in } \Omega,\qquad A(x)\nabla u\cdot\nu + b(x)\, u = g(x) \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega,
$$
where $A\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^{N\times N})$ is uniformly elliptic, $a_0 \in L^{r_1}(\Omega)$, $b \in L^{r_2}(\partial\Omega)$ are nonnegative, and the data satisfy $f \in L^q(\Omega)$, $g \in L^{q_*}(\partial\Omega)$ with $q > N/2$ and $q_* > N-1$. Define the symmetric form
$$
a_S(u,v) = \int_\Omega A\nabla u\cdot \nabla v\, dx + \int_\Omega a_0\, u v\, dx + \int_{\partial\Omega} b\, u v\, d\sigma,
$$
with form domain $D(a_S) \subset H^1(\Omega)$, and assume the Sobolev-type embedding $D(a_S)\hookrightarrow L^p(\Omega)$ for the optimal exponent $p$ (so that $p = 2N/(N-2)$ when $N\ge 3$). Let $q^{**}$ be the exponent obtained by combining this embedding with the Moser iteration scheme applied to weak solutions of the above problem, yielding a priori bounds of the form
$$
\|u\|_{L^{q^{**}}(\Omega)} \le C\bigl(\|f\|_{L^q(\Omega)} + \|g\|_{L^{q_*}(\partial\Omega)}\bigr).
$$
Question: is the exponent $q^{**}$ in this a priori bound optimal, in the sense that no larger exponent can be inserted on the left-hand side under the same hypotheses on $f$, $g$, $a_0$, $b$?
artifact.status_search_result: The evidence accompanying the question explicitly states that the resulting $L^{q^{**}}$ a priori bounds are best possible, with optimality established through a known result of Daners (Theorem 5.11 of his 2000 work on Robin boundary value problems on Lipschitz domains). The question is therefore resolved affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Robin boundary value problems on arbitrary domains (Daners)
status_evidence.snippet: Daners (2000), Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 352, establishes sharp a priori L^p estimates for solutions of Robin problems, including optimality of the resulting integrability exponents.
status_evidence.claim: The optimality of the L^{q**} a priori bounds for the generalized Robin problem is established (Daners, Theorem 5.11).
